headline: Raising IGF-1
punch: One trial moved it with no GH change.

headline: The chain everyone recites
subhead: GH UP, IGF-1 UP, HEIGHT UP
body: So the chain is GH rises, IGF-1 rises, height follows. Which carries a hidden implication nobody states: that the only way to move IGF-1 is to move GH first, and therefore the only lever worth pulling is the GH one. | A 2025 trial in short-stature children broke that link in a way worth looking at carefully, because it got the IGF-1 rise without the GH rise, and it did it with no drug at all.
punch: You can move one without the other.

headline: Twenty-four weeks of jumping
body: Short-stature children split into three groups. One group did a structured jumping programme for **24 weeks**. The other two were observed over the same period with no intervention, which gives you two separate controls rather than one. | Then they measured height, GH, IGF-1 and IGFBP-3 in all three groups, before and after. A real intervention with real controls and a real duration, which is more than most exercise studies manage.
punch: A real intervention with real controls.

headline: What happened to their height?
body: The exercise group finished with **higher height, higher serum IGF-1**, and a higher IGF-1 to IGFBP-3 molar ratio than both control groups, all at **p < 0.05** against the untreated group. | So a purely mechanical intervention moved the hormone that everyone treats as something you can only change pharmacologically. No injection, no compound, and the axis moved.

headline: And the GH did not move
body: Here is the finding that makes this worth a post. There was **no significant difference in serum GH** between the groups, before or after, at **p > 0.05**. | The IGF-1 went up. The height went up. The GH did not change. So whatever raised the IGF-1 in those children did not do it by routing through a bigger GH signal, which is the only mechanism the standard chain allows for.

headline: Why would GH stay flat?
body: It fits because tissues manufacture their own IGF-1 locally, and they do it in response to mechanical load as well as hormonal signal. Bone and cartilage both respond to being loaded, independently of what the endocrine system is doing that day. | So you can raise the IGF-1 that actually matters without raising the GH that supposedly controls it. Which is the same lesson every direct-action experiment in this series taught, arrived at from the opposite direction.
punch: Load is a second input to the same axis.

headline: Be precise about the limits
body: This is 24 weeks in short-stature children, not years and not adults. Height differences over six months are small and partly just normal growth happening, which the controls help with but do not eliminate. | And the statistically significant comparison was specifically against Group 3, not uniformly across every group comparison. The honest read is a real effect on the axis with a short follow-up, not a demonstration that jumping makes you tall.
punch: One trial, six months, modest effect.

headline: What this changes
body: The GH to IGF-1 chain is not one-directional and GH is not its only input. Loading raised IGF-1 with GH flat, in a controlled trial, in the population you would most want to test it in. | Which lands in the same place as the injection studies: the IGF-1 that matters is made locally, and more than one thing controls how much of it gets made.
punch: ==The axis has more than one lever.==
